summary: HavenRetail: heartbeat-fanout storm caused streaming silence, duplicate completions and billing exposure
description: Issue summary: During peak window 2026-03-10 07:40-08:20 UTC a correlated set of heartbeat events from HavenRetail sessions caused a scheduler fanout amplification. This resulted in large numbers of ephemeral session requeues, stalled streaming frames (silence) for affected customers and a subset of requests being retried to the legacy multiplexer which produced duplicate completions. Impact: customer-facing streaming silence on session-based chat features, visible spike in 5xx and 429s, and a billing exposure for duplicate token charges. Timeline: first alert 07:42 UTC, escalation to SRE 07:50 UTC, mitigation rollbacks started 08:05 UTC, services stabilized 08:18 UTC, post-incident review started 2026-03-11.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate 10k concurrent short-lived sessions using heartbeat interval 2s and rapid connect/disconnect churn
2) Route requests through the scheduler with fanout enabled and per-session priority unset
3) Observe scheduler requeues and streaming connection stalls when ephemeral queue grows above threshold
4) Verify duplicate completions by replaying traffic against the legacy multiplexer during a partial fallback window

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: network partition caused scheduler retries — disproven after infra network checks showed no packet loss in us-east cluster
Found that a recent scheduler change (PR#10823) modified fanout backpressure logic; under rapid heartbeat churn the backpressure threshold calculation became non-monotonic
When backpressure miscomputed, scheduler re-enqueued sessions aggressively which saturated the serving-runtime incoming queue and starved streaming goroutines
Legacy multiplexer fallback was triggered for a percentage of affected requests; fallback logic did not properly deduplicate in the transient window leading to duplicate completions
Billing system logs show ~0.6% of HavenRetail tokens were double-counted between 07:42 and 08:18 UTC — estimated invoice exposure is under review by Finance

resolution: Root cause: regression in scheduler fanout backpressure introduced in PR#10823 that under rapid heartbeat churn caused requeue amplification and serving-runtime queue starvation. Fixes applied: immediate rollback of PR#10823 during incident; follow-on patch PR#10911 implements monotonic backpressure calculation, adds per-customer fanout limiter, and strengthens fallback deduplication. Customer mitigation: HavenRetail was notified and provided a provisional 30% credit for affected window; Finance to finalize reconciliation. Follow-ups assigned (see action_items).
